title: Building a finite ring extension that realizes a prescribed isomorphism modulo a fixed power of a nonzerodivisor
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma starts from a finite ring extension A' contained in A with a nonzerodivisor f satisfying A'_f = A_f, and asserts the existence of an integer n_0 such that for every n at least n_0, every isomorphism A'/f^nA' -> B'/g^nB' carrying f to g can be extended to a finite ring extension B' contained in B together with a ring isomorphism A/fA -> B/gB compatible with it (statement lines 35690-35700). The proof is constructive and not a formal consequence of its hypotheses: the first move extracts an exponent t with f^tA contained in A' and then sets n_0 = 2t, after which the module B is manufactured from the congruence condition that defines N and from B = g^{-t}N, and the two inclusions g^tB' contained in N and N N contained in g^tN are what make B a ring extending B' (proof lines 35703-35713). Finiteness is then read off from the displayed isomorphism A/f^tA' -> B/g^tB' and from the finiteness of A/f^tA' over A' (proof lines 35714-35720). The author ends by leaving the final compatibility verification of the displayed isomorphism to the reader, a residual check that is routine and that is preserved verbatim in the counted span; the construction itself, which is the substance of the proof, is fully present.
